tier_reason: First-party design memo gives numbers against BIND 9.9.2 (>180Kqps vs 41K qps, queryperf-like tool, one core of a 2.20GHz AMD64 machine) and says the jinmei-l1cache branch was 'more than 4 times faster than BIND 9'. The benchmarked code is not public in this repo, and there is no compiler, flags or CPU model, so it cannot be A; not peer-reviewed, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Experimental cache-only server with fully-rendered cached data: 'over 180Kqps' vs 'just 41K qps' for BIND 9.9.2 (queryperf-like benchmark, single core, 2.20GHz AMD64), about 4.4x (derived from page data). The same memo says the jinmei-l1cache branch 'ran vary [sic] fast; more than 4 times faster than BIND 9, and even much faster than other implementations that have full response cache (although, as usual, the comparison is not entirely fair)'.
corrections.workload: Recursive-resolver cache-hit path (not authoritative serving): experimental cache-only implementation (jinmei-l1cache branch) using a hash table keyed by (query name, type) that stores the fully rendered wire-format answer section (minimal-responses) plus RR offsets for TTL update/rotation; max response throughput measured with a queryperf-like tool on one core against BIND 9.9.2.
corrections.hardware: One test machine, 2.20GHz AMD64, single core used; CPU model not named
corrections.is_fork_of: BIND 10 (ISC) - Bundy is its community continuation per README (not a GitHub fork)
corrections.caveats: First-party design-memo claim (doc/design/resolver/03-cache-algorithm, committed 2013, benchmark against BIND 9.9.2) with no compiler, flags or CPU model. The author says the experimental implementation 'skips some necessary features for a production server', that a production version 'wouldn't be that fast', and that the comparison is 'not entirely fair'. The jinmei-l1cache branch is not among the 21 branches of bundy-dns/bundy and GitHub code search finds 'l1cache' only in this design doc, so the benchmarked code is not public; shipped Bundy has no such speed claim. README declares the project in 'hibernation' (no active development, no security fixes, not recommended for production); the last code commit is 2017-05-10 and the 2026 commits only edit README.org. License: ISC core; bundled ext/asio and ext/coroutine are BSL-1.0.

notes: Record understated the page: exact qps figures (>180Kqps vs 41K qps for BIND 9.9.2) are present, and the workload is a recursive-resolver cache, not an authoritative path. maintenance_status left 'active' by the last-commit rule (2026-03-18), but those commits are README-only and README says 'hibernation'; orchestrator may prefer 'abandoned' (last code commit 2017). has_code left true (repo has DNS code) but the benchmarked l1cache code is not public; consider has_code=false for this variant. The memo's cited list link lists.bundy.org is dead (DNS failure); the ISC copy of the related 2012 bind10-dev post has no qps numbers.

tier_reason: Author's own blog post runs a public libtest benchmark (server/benches/comparison_benches.rs, PR #317; now bin/benches/comparison.rs) against BIND 9.11, and the linked config.log gist gives BIND's compiler and flags. No CPU model and no rustc version are stated, so it is not A; first-party, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Single UDP A query for www.example.com: 68,173 ns/iter (+/- 11,699) for TRust-DNS vs 69,576 ns/iter (+/- 3,620) for BIND9 (9.11 per the linked config.log gist), about 2% lower median round-trip time (derived from page data), inside TRust-DNS's reported +/- spread. Starting point was 400us vs 100us; after the bench was fixed to launch a release instead of a debug binary it was 79,274 vs 69,960 ns/iter before the optimizations.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: TRust-DNS: Rust nightly libtest bench (rustc version not stated), release build. BIND 9.11: default ./configure with Apple LLVM 7.3.0 (clang-703.0.29) as gcc, CFLAGS -g -O2 (from the linked config.log gist)
corrections.hardware: Author's 'getting older laptop' on macOS (x86_64; BIND build host Darwin 16.1.0 per config.log gist); no CPU model
corrections.caveats: Author says 'I'm not being scientific here'. Hardware is only 'my getting older laptop' on macOS, with no CPU model; rustc nightly version not stated. BIND is 9.11 (linked config.log gist, default -g -O2). The ~1.4us win is inside TRust-DNS's +/-11,699 ns spread; the author notes macOS updates during the month cost both servers ~5us, and that BIND9 has more features and TRust-DNS may not be faster for TCP, dynamic update or DNSSEC signing. Post dated 2017-12-29, so it does not reflect current Hickory or BIND. Benchmark code is public: server/benches/comparison_benches.rs (PR #317, merged 2017-12-31); the current repo has bin/benches/comparison.rs.

notes: Numbers verified verbatim. Record said no BIND version was pinned, but the post links a config.log gist showing BIND 9.11 built with Apple LLVM 7.3.0 at -g -O2; compiler_and_flags, hardware and caveats updated. The 'win' is effectively parity within noise; metadata (MIT OR Apache-2.0 via Cargo.toml, 5,429 stars, last commit 2026-09-26) checks out.

tier_reason: First-party Changelog entry (22 February 2008, Wouter) lists cache-hit qps for BIND and Unbound and states 'about 3.4x faster than BIND in cache performance'. There is no BIND version, compiler, flags, CPU model or named load tool, so C.
notes: All numbers match doc/Changelog verbatim (BIND 8987.99 vs Ub 31218.3; DO bit BIND 8269.31 vs Ub 28735.6 qps; NSD 35182.8 vs Ub 36048.4), and the 3.4x ratio is stated on the page, not derived. The repo has testcode/perf.c ('estimates DNS name server performance') but the entry does not say it was used. Metadata checks out: BSD-3-Clause, 4,942 stars, last commit 2026-09-22, not archived.
